A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe Mocap-2-to-3, and their main text, equations, figures and tables are readable. All 10 pages of v3 and 9 pages of v4 were inspected. Neither contains appendices or embedded supplements, although v4 references Appendices B.2 and B.3, limiting comparison of camera configuration and geometric derivation details.

before.justification: v3 reports original RICH and AIST++ evaluations, qualitative reconstructions, and pointmap and 2D-pretraining ablations in Section 4 and Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v4 reports original benchmark results, motion-quality measurements, qualitative reconstructions, and expanded component and convergence ablations in Section 4 and Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: The two-stage diffusion, view attention, pointmaps, triangulation and SMPLify pipeline persists. However, v4 specifies J−1 non-root local joints and J+1 total output slots, versus J local joints and J+2 slots in v3, and replaces the reconstruction factor (scale+1)/2 with s. The PDFs do not establish whether these differences reflect an implemented parameterization change or clarified bookkeeping and normalization.

E1.justification: The evaluation datasets and SMPL/COCO lifting tasks remain RICH and AIST++. Training coverage expands modestly: v3 explicitly excludes AIST++ training data, whereas v4 Table 2 adds an AIST++ 2D-pretraining variant while retaining a variant without that data. The other named training datasets remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v4 adds WHAM+SMPLify to the RICH comparison and extends qualitative comparisons to optimized baselines. GVHMR+SMPLify was already evaluated in v3 and is not a new comparator. The AIST++ baseline set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v4 substantially broadens evaluation with Accel, Jitter and foot-sliding metrics on RICH, a 3500-versus-8000-epoch pointmap convergence comparison, and additional decoupling and AIST++ pretraining controls. Existing pose and trajectory metrics remain. The complete training schedule is no longer supplied, so changed benchmark scores cannot be assumed to come from otherwise identical settings.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds a control without pose/global-motion decoupling and an extended-training control without pointmaps, directly testing representation necessity and convergence speed. Table 2 adds the effect of AIST++ 2D pretraining. New failure illustrations and AIST++ qualitative cases supplement the retained RICH analyses, substantially strengthening investigation of the method's components and behavior.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added epoch counts describe training duration, not statistical replication or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: RICH Table 1 changes Ours PA-MPJPE/MPJPE/Abs-MPJPE from 25.8/38.7/152.5 to 26.2/39.6/156.8, and W-MPJPE/WA-MPJPE from 85.3/56.1 to 82.6/50.1. Several baseline scores also change. New motion-quality results show foot sliding of 3.5 for Ours versus 2.5 for GVHMR. AIST++ and ablation results are expanded and revised, including a new pretraining variant. These are revised or added results, not established same-setting gains. v4's prose gives Abs-MPJPE as 111.5 mm, conflicting with Table 1's 156.8 mm.

T1.justification: Neither readable main text introduces a theorem or proof. v3 explicitly presents the ground-plane equation and coordinate-construction reasoning; v4 summarizes the geometry and defers its computation to unavailable Appendix B.3. It is therefore unclear whether that derivation was moved unchanged or revised. The changed root and scale notation alone does not establish a substantive mathematical change.

C1.justification: The central claims about 2D pretraining, multi-view lifting, generalization and absolute positioning persist. v4 newly characterizes absolute-depth recovery as a novel task and foregrounds accelerated trajectory convergence as a contribution of ground-plane conditioning. These refine the claimed novelty and component roles without replacing the paper's central contribution.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly interprets pointmaps as accelerating convergence rather than being essential for eventual learning, based on the longer-training control. It attributes worse foot sliding than GVHMR to omitted post-processing and adds detection-confidence, foot-sliding and SLAM-based future directions. Detector-quality and calibrated-camera applicability constraints remain, although their presentation changes.

D1.justification: The supplied v4 omits v3 Section 4.1's architecture dimensions, Adam optimizer, learning rates, batch sizes, two-stage epoch schedule and maximum sequence length. It newly identifies a ResNet-18 pointmap encoder and lists camera augmentation parameters, but camera and pointmap details also point to missing appendices. This substantially changes the available reproducibility information without proving that the omitted settings changed. Both versions still promise a future code release.

R1.justification: Related work expands to discuss HMMR, DSD, SLAHMR, PACE, PromptHMR, HumanMM and TRAM/ZoeDepth, adding distinctions concerning drift, computation and input requirements. The basic positioning relative to Motion-2-to-3, MAS and MVLift remains. Hartley–Sturm and MonoUni citations disappear, while triangulation now cites Wikipedia. MVLift remains the same cited work despite changed bibliographic attribution.

P1.justification: v4 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, method explanation and experimental discussion. Motion representation moves after pretraining and fine-tuning, pointmap conditioning becomes a separate convergence section, and limitations merge into the conclusion. The title, author list, affiliations and citation style also change. This is substantial narrative and structural revision.

P2.justification: The overview and pipeline figures are redrawn, the pointmap illustration is redesigned, and a new representation/failure diagram appears. The former combined RICH qualitative figure becomes expanded separate comparisons, and AIST++ gains a qualitative figure. Table 1 becomes a grouped full-width display with motion-quality columns and camera-input markers; the tables also gain result highlighting and revised structures.

improvement.justification: v4 improves empirical scrutiny through direct decoupling and convergence controls, motion-quality measurements and an additional optimized baseline. However, the supplied revision loses much of v3's reproducibility information, refers to unavailable appendices, and contains an Abs-MPJPE discrepancy between prose and Table 1. These evidential gains and documentation/reporting losses, together with unclear settings behind revised scores, prevent a reliable judgment of net overall quality.
